observation: DSeq-JEPA v4 Table 4 (p.11, ViT-B/16, ImageNet linear probe / iNat21) reports: uniform+flat (= I-JEPA) 72.4/35.9; uniform+sequential 72.3/34.9; discriminative+flat 72.0/35.7; discriminative+sequential 73.5/36.4. The accompanying text assigns the rows explicitly, and Table 5 (which fixes the discriminative region set and varies only order) lists Flat = 72.0, corroborating the row assignment.
interpretation: Importance-guided region selection combined with a FLAT (parallel) predictor - the configuration our system implements - scores BELOW the uniform I-JEPA baseline in the authors' own ablation. DSeq-JEPA therefore does not support the premise that important-region masking alone should improve a parallel JEPA; its gain is attributed to selection AND sequential conditioning acting together.
limits: Single-run cells; the paper reports 3-seed stability (73.8 +/- 0.4) only for the headline configuration, so the 0.4-point gap is within that spread. Direction only, no significance claim. Nothing here says our AUC results are correct or that our code is defect-free.
requested_action: coordinator: this is the citation that answers the 'MAE and DSeq-JEPA prove masking important regions should work' premise; mask/training owners: see Q1-Q3 in literature_matrix.md section 5.

observation: DSeq-JEPA context construction, read in official code (src/frameworks/dseqjepa/pretrain.py:36-55, 418-446): keep-sets are the cumulative union of the already-seen top-ranked regions; targets are regions[:,1:], i.e. R2..RN, and R_N is the complement/background produced by attention.py:87-90. The top-ranked region R1 is never a prediction target. Encoder input is restricted to those salient regions via masked attention (comment at pretrain.py:398/426), not by token dropping.
interpretation: DSeq-JEPA SHOWS the most discriminative tissue to the encoder and predicts progressively less-salient regions from it, ending on background. Our guided arms do the reverse: they hide guide-positive tissue and predict it from the remainder. The two designs are structurally opposite on this axis, so DSeq-JEPA's gains cannot be transferred to our intervention by analogy.
limits: Read-only inspection; no execution of their code. Also noted (observation, not a claim about their results): generate_dseq_masks unions prev_masks BEFORE appending the current region, so keep-sets appear as [R1, R1, R1uR2, R1uR2uR3] for targets [R2, R3, R4, R5] - one step behind Eq. (5).

observation: MAE 2111.06377v3 Table 1f (p.5): random 75% = 84.9 ft / 73.5 lin, block 50% = 83.9/72.3, block 75% = 82.8/63.9, grid 75% = 84.0/66.0; the paper's own conclusion is that simple random sampling works best (p.6). SemMAE 2206.10207v3 Table 3 (p.7, ViT-B 8x8, linear probe): random 66.8; mask 75% patches per part 66.5; mask 75% PARTS 52.9; adaptive schedules 63.3-68.7 with best at gamma=2 (68.7); Table 4: iBOT-derived parts 63.6 vs baseline 63.7 vs learned parts 65.0. I-JEPA 2301.08243v3 Tables 8-11 (pp.14-15): target scale (0.15,0.2)=54.2 best; context scale 0.40->31.2, 0.65->47.1, 0.75->49.3, 0.85->54.2; target count 1/2/3/4 -> 9.0/22.0/48.5/54.2; masking teacher OUTPUT 67.3 vs INPUT 56.1. Anatomically-guided MAE 2502.21244v1 Table 3 (p.8): anatomy-biased masking alone (E) beats plain MAE (F) on all four evaluation sets, but the authors attribute the largest single gain to artery-intersecting crop SAMPLING, and plain MAE pretraining (F) underperforms no pretraining (G) on three of four sets.
interpretation: Original MAE is random-masking; guided variants are separate works with mixed results. Whole-region masking without a schedule is strongly negative in SemMAE. Guide quality, not the idea of guidance, carried SemMAE's gain. I-JEPA's context-scale table is the strongest published support for the author's 'informative context' clause.
limits: AnatMAE Table 3 prints four column labels over three checkmark columns; row readings follow the surrounding text, not the glyphs. SemMAE official code not read. No work in this set evaluates frozen-probe volume-level medical classification.

observation: Coordinator review identified seven overclaims in the first version of literature_matrix.md and terminology.md. All were errors of inference by this agent, not source errors; no table value or quoted phrase changed. Corrections: (1) DSeq Table 4 cell is an ANALOGOUS FACTOR COMBINATION, not our exact configuration - differences enumerated (CLS-similarity saliency, Otsu/connected-component irregular non-overlapping regions, complement R_N, masked-attention conditioning, ImageNet, last-4-block-concat linear probe); numbers retained with NO significance conclusion; 'their gain needs sequencing' replaced by their own attribution in their construction. (2) r_max=1 equated to SemMAE alpha=1 - removed; per-pred-block placement coin vs part-level mask-count interpolation are different interventions. (3) 'Nobody in this set runs 100% guided with a parallel predictor' - removed as self-contradicting (AnatMAE is permanently guided and parallel; SemMAE ends at its whole-part endpoint). (4) I-JEPA venue corrected to CVPR 2023 with the arXiv comment quoted and flagged. (5) Our guides are not fixed precomputed bitmaps: CENTROID is computed from each transformed image; the cached MIRAGE envelope is transformed jointly with its image. Arm counting corrected to five policy families / six implementations (ANATOMY v1 and v2; COVER delivered_v2 exists under the mask owner and keeps a distinct label). Manuscript DOES report fine-tuning diagnostics (main_submission.tex section 'Fine-tuning narrows the observed gap', tab:finetuned) - the global 'we do not report fine-tuning' claim removed. Context vocabulary expanded to three named sets: candidate context block, target complement, delivered context. (6) DSeq R_1 described as highest-saliency-ranked region on natural images, not 'most discriminative tissue'; structural contrast restated at factor level with no inverted analogy; official code paths corrected to src/frameworks/dseqjepa/pretrain.py and attention.py (no root-level pretrain.py exists); the Eq.5-vs-code one-step lag marked UNCERTAIN, non-actionable, and explicitly not a basis for changing our sampler. (7) New prohibition: low-shot ImageNet numbers are not evidence about learned anatomical importance; the I-JEPA context-scale finding is retained but bounded to its own sampler and benchmark.
interpretation: Both owned documents are now safe for narrow citation. Sections 7 (source/inference boundary) and 8 (corrections log) were added to literature_matrix.md so the superseded version is not cited by mistake.
limits: No new literature crawl was performed; no source was re-read except the arXiv metadata recheck. No manuscript, bib, code, commit, push or training-authority change. Corrections are to my three owned files only.
